facts_of_case: The respondent/wife filed a divorce petition under Section 13 (I) (i-a) and (i-b) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 on grounds of cruelty and desertion, and for maintenance under Section 25 of the Hindu Marriage Act. The case was about the wife's allegations of cruelty and desertion by her husband.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking divorce to prove that the marriage has been dissolved.
legal_principles.held: Although there was no objection filed by the appellant, the Family Court proceeded to record the oral testimony of the respondent as PW1 and marked Exts.A1 to A7 documents on her side.

legal_principles.principle: A party cannot rely on a subsequent remarriage to contend that an appeal against the grant of divorce has become infructuous.
legal_principles.held: As regards the award of permanent maintenance to the respondent by the court below, the learned counsel would submit that the award of such a huge amount towards permanent maintenance came about solely because the appellant did not get an effective opportunity to adduce evidence before the court below.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed. The judgment of the trial court is set aside, and the matter is remitted to the trial court for fresh disposal.
